3use core::marker::PhantomData;
4use core::ptr::{drop_in_place, NonNull};
5
6extern crate alloc;
7
8use alloc::alloc::{dealloc, Layout};
9
10// Self referential structs are currently not supported with safe vanilla Rust.
11// The only reasonable safe alternative is to expect the user to juggle 2 separate
12// data structures which is a mess. The library solution rental is both no longer
13// maintained and really heavy to compile. So begrudgingly I rolled my own version.
14// These are some of the core invariants we require for this to be safe to use.
15//
16// 1. owner is initialized when UnsafeSelfCell is constructed.
17// 2. owner is NEVER changed again.
18// 3. The pointer to owner and dependent never changes, even when moved.
19// 4. The only access to owner and dependent is as immutable reference.
20// 5. owner lives longer than dependent.
21
22#[doc(hidden)]
23pub struct JoinedCell<Owner, Dependent> {
24    pub owner: Owner,
25    pub dependent: Dependent,
26}
27
28// Library controlled struct that marks all accesses as unsafe.
29// Because the macro generated struct impl can be extended, could be unsafe.
30#[doc(hidden)]
31pub struct UnsafeSelfCell<ContainedIn, Owner, DependentStatic: 'static> {
32    joined_void_ptr: NonNull<u8>,
33
34    // ContainedIn is necessary for type safety since we don't fully
35    // prohibit access to the UnsafeSelfCell; swapping between different
36    // structs can be unsafe otherwise, see Issue #17.
37    contained_in_marker: PhantomData<ContainedIn>,
38
39    owner_marker: PhantomData<Owner>,
40    // DependentStatic is only used to correctly derive Send and Sync.
41    dependent_marker: PhantomData<DependentStatic>,
42}
43
44impl<ContainedIn, Owner, DependentStatic> UnsafeSelfCell<ContainedIn, Owner, DependentStatic> {
45    pub unsafe fn new(joined_void_ptr: NonNull<u8>) -> Self {
46        Self {
47            joined_void_ptr,
48            contained_in_marker: PhantomData,
49            owner_marker: PhantomData,
50            dependent_marker: PhantomData,
51        }
52    }
53
54    // Calling any of these *unsafe* functions with the wrong Dependent type is UB.
55
56    pub unsafe fn borrow_dependent<'a, Dependent>(&'a self) -> &'a Dependent {
57        let joined_ptr = self.joined_void_ptr.cast::<JoinedCell<Owner, Dependent>>();
58
59        &(*joined_ptr.as_ptr()).dependent
60    }
61
62    pub unsafe fn borrow_mut<'a, Dependent>(&'a mut self) -> (&'a Owner, &'a mut Dependent) {
63        let joined_ptr = self.joined_void_ptr.cast::<JoinedCell<Owner, Dependent>>();
64
65        // This function used to return `&'a mut JoinedCell<Owner, Dependent>`.
66        // It now creates two references to the fields instead to avoid claiming mutable access
67        // to the whole `JoinedCell` (including the owner!) here.
68        (
69            &(*joined_ptr.as_ptr()).owner,
70            &mut (*joined_ptr.as_ptr()).dependent,
71        )
72    }
73
74    // Any subsequent use of this struct other than dropping it is UB.
75    pub unsafe fn drop_joined<Dependent>(&mut self) {
76        let joined_ptr = self.joined_void_ptr.cast::<JoinedCell<Owner, Dependent>>();
77
78        // Also used in case drop_in_place(...dependent) fails
79        let _guard = OwnerAndCellDropGuard { joined_ptr };
80
81        // IMPORTANT dependent must be dropped before owner.
82        // We don't want to rely on an implicit order of struct fields.
83        // So we drop the struct, field by field manually.
84        drop_in_place(&mut (*joined_ptr.as_ptr()).dependent);
85
86        // Dropping owner
87        // and deallocating
88        // due to _guard at end of scope.
89    }
90}
91
92unsafe impl<ContainedIn, Owner, DependentStatic> Send
93    for UnsafeSelfCell<ContainedIn, Owner, DependentStatic>
94where
95    // Only derive Send if Owner and DependentStatic is also Send
96    Owner: Send,
97    DependentStatic: Send,
98{
99}

101unsafe impl<ContainedIn, Owner, DependentStatic> Sync
102    for UnsafeSelfCell<ContainedIn, Owner, DependentStatic>
103where
104    // Only derive Sync if Owner and DependentStatic is also Sync
105    Owner: Sync,
106    DependentStatic: Sync,
107{

110// This struct is used to safely deallocate only the owner if dependent
111// construction fails.
112//
113// mem::forget it once it's no longer needed or dtor will be UB.
114#[doc(hidden)]
115pub struct OwnerAndCellDropGuard<Owner, Dependent> {
116    joined_ptr: NonNull<JoinedCell<Owner, Dependent>>,
117}
118
119impl<Owner, Dependent> OwnerAndCellDropGuard<Owner, Dependent> {
120    pub unsafe fn new(joined_ptr: NonNull<JoinedCell<Owner, Dependent>>) -> Self {
121        Self { joined_ptr }
122    }
123}
124
125impl<Owner, Dependent> Drop for OwnerAndCellDropGuard<Owner, Dependent> {
126    fn drop(&mut self) {
127        struct DeallocGuard {
128            ptr: *mut u8,
129            layout: Layout,
130        }
131        impl Drop for DeallocGuard {
132            fn drop(&mut self) {
133                unsafe { dealloc(self.ptr, self.layout) }
134            }
135        }
136
137        // Deallocate even when the drop_in_place(...owner) panics
138        let _guard = DeallocGuard {
139            ptr: self.joined_ptr.as_ptr() as *mut u8,
140            layout: Layout::new::<JoinedCell<Owner, Dependent>>(),
141        };
142
143        unsafe {
144            // We must only drop owner and the struct itself,
145            // The whole point of this drop guard is to clean up the partially
146            // initialized struct should building the dependent fail.
147            drop_in_place(&mut (*self.joined_ptr.as_ptr()).owner);
148        }
149
150        // Deallocation happens at end of scope
151    }
152}
153
154// Because of 'procedural macros cannot expand to macro definitions' we wrap
155// field pointer acquisition in a helper function.
156impl<Owner, Dependent> JoinedCell<Owner, Dependent> {
157    #[doc(hidden)]
158    pub unsafe fn _field_pointers(this: *mut Self) -> (*mut Owner, *mut Dependent) {
159        let owner_ptr = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!((*this).owner);
160        let dependent_ptr = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!((*this).dependent);
161
162        (owner_ptr, dependent_ptr)
163    }
164}
